script: Most difficult paths in Champions League history. People love arguing about which Champions League winner had the easiest road, but Barcelona in the 2014-2015 season had the exact opposite. Their run kicked off in the round of sixteen against Manchester City, where Luis Suarez scored twice inside the first 30 minutes at the Etihad before Ivan Rakitic settled the tie in the second leg back in Spain for a 3-1 aggregate win. But knocking out City was somehow the gentlest part of what came next. Next came Paris Saint-Germain in the quarter-final, where Neymar and Suarez pulled them apart across two legs for a 5-1 win that included a Neymar double in the return game. Then it was Bayern Munich in the semi-final, and at the Camp Nou, Lionel Messi delivered one of the greatest individual displays the competition has ever seen, including that goal where he sat Jerome Boateng on the floor. Barca took the tie 5-3 and reached the final in Berlin. But if you line up all four of these opponents side by side, you'll see the pattern that makes this run almost impossible to repeat, and if you're enjoying the video, please hit the follow button. Barcelona beat Juventus 3-1 to lift the trophy and seal the treble, and here's the part almost nobody points out. Manchester City were the reigning Premier League champions when Barca knocked them out. PSG were the reigning champions of Ligue 1, Bayern held the Bundesliga crown, and Juventus were the sitting Serie A champions. So in a single run, Barcelona knocked out the reigning champion of England, France, Germany, and Italy, one after another.
